items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the story 'The Address', and answer.

"The woman opened the door only a few inches. She looked at the visitor without a flicker of recognition. 'I don't know you,' she said. But the visitor had already noticed the green cardigan with the wooden buttons – a cardigan her own mother had knitted. The door closed. The visitor stood on the step, her hand still raised, and then walked slowly back to the station."

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the story 'The Address', and answer.

"The silver candlestick stood on the sideboard, polished and gleaming. At home it had stood by the window every Friday, and her mother had lit it while the soup simmered. Here it was only an ornament between a vase and a clock. She found she did not want to touch it. Everything she had come to see was here, and none of it was hers any more."

Which theme of "The Address" does this passage reflect?
items.answer: Objects lose meaning when cut off from the life they belonged to.
